notes.title: The Empty Hook
notes.author: Old Moss — journal scrap
notes.placement: A lantern bracket rubbing, beneath a proposed broken clay rim in the southeast corner.
notes.body: The hook is sound. The glass is sound. I have cleaned both twice. What is missing is the little line of light that used to reach them. I shall check the next marker tomorrow. If that fails, I shall ask for help.

notes.title: A Quiet Visitor
notes.author: F. — folded leaf
notes.placement: Folded leaf in the northern dead end; expose one pale corner around the last turn.
notes.body: I waited in the leaves while a snake passed so close that I could count the scales beneath his chin. He did not see me. Then I moved to get a better look. An experiment with a clear result.

notes.body: Mend west wall. Find missing trowel. Mend west wall. Find out who is writing mend west wall on every page. It is my handwriting. This makes the matter harder to take up with anyone.

notes.placement: A folded storage label at the northwest wall; proposed small wall-mounted paper sleeve.
notes.body: One copy in the shelter. One with the keeper. Never leave both on the same shelf. The well keeper hid his behind the thin, cracked hedge southeast of the Garden Ruins. I hope he remembers which bit. All hedges look rather alike from down here.

notes.title: What the River Kept
notes.author: Reed — bark rubbing
notes.placement: Bark strip at the northeast room corner, above the drawn floor waterline; no new swim required.
notes.body: Before the water rose, I copied the little feet on the old crossing. They point beneath the river, not along it. I cannot tell whether this is a road that drowned or a road that knew the water was coming.

notes.title: Reach, Then Think
notes.author: F. — practice scrap
notes.placement: Practice scrap along the inside wall of the lower east room, outside the actual key tile.
notes.body: A tongue is splendid for fetching something from the far bank. Less splendid for fetching yourself after it. Before reaching for the key, I now make certain I know where my feet will go next. This is a recent improvement.

notes.title: The Return Passage
notes.author: Brass — repair docket
notes.placement: Repair docket against the east wall of the lower room; collectable before touching the key.
notes.body: The doors were built in pairs. When one closes, look for the passage its mechanism has released. Do not spend the whole afternoon arguing with the closed one. I did that yesterday. The open passage was behind me.

notes.placement: Small rubbing in the one-exit pocket just southeast of centre, not on a reaction trigger.
notes.body: The return route is marked on the back. If the front is damaged, turn the sheet over. If both sides are damaged, leave a fresh mark where you found the trouble. Someone smaller may be following you.

notes.title: First Lesson
notes.author: F. — practice book leaf
notes.placement: Practice leaf in the small western dead end; only the paper edge is visible from its entrance.
notes.body: I asked when I would be taught the secret of being a Wayfinder. My teacher told me to sit beside a snake and watch which way it turned. I asked again the next day. Same snake. Same answer.

notes.author: F. — trial archive slip
notes.placement: Trial record at the northeast corner of the upper room; proposed scuffed slate on wall edge.
notes.body: The old burrow north of the Garden Ruins opens to care, not coins: one perfect escape in each of five different areas. I thought five perfect escapes in one area would do. The door and I have agreed to disagree. — F.

notes.author: Dusty — clay-roof sketch
notes.placement: Roof sketch at the northeast corner of the upper chamber, away from a scorpion spawn.
notes.body: The first little roof was for the glow bugs. The second was for the keeper who tended them. By noon everyone wanted a roof, including the scorpion. I made his a little farther from the others.

notes.author: F. — sand-stained scrap
notes.placement: Sand-stained scrap at the north edge of the western room, requiring a lateral turn.
notes.body: The raised tail is a warning, not an invitation to hurry straight past. I step out of the marked sting, wait, then move. I have underlined wait because that was the part I kept leaving out.

notes.author: Murk — bark label
notes.placement: Bark label at the northeast wall corner; a short look behind the room edge reveals it.
notes.body: The roots lifted this path by half a shell-length. I changed the drawing. The next spring they lifted it again. If your map and the garden disagree, look at both before deciding which one is being difficult.

notes.title: A Better Way to Listen
notes.author: F. — folded reed
notes.placement: Rolled reed in the narrow northern pocket near the eastern half; not in a frog spawn.
notes.body: A stone makes a noise where it lands. In these halls, a frog may make the next noise somewhere else. Watch where the hunters actually go. They have not promised to follow the first sound you meant them to hear.

notes.author: Old Moss — relay label
notes.placement: Dry relay label along the west interior wall of a lower room; proposed bark flap, no added collision.
notes.body: These sheets belong to the path, not the shelter. If the roof falls, move them somewhere dry and leave a mark. Do not take them all home for safekeeping. A perfectly safe map that nobody can find is a very poor map.

notes.placement: Parcel label at the southwest corner near the start-side room; an easy discovery after the harder first jungle note.
notes.body: Left three berries here for the next traveller. Returned to find two berries and a thank-you scratched into the bark. I had rather expected an empty parcel. It is pleasant to be wrong about someone.

notes.title: The Part That Answers
notes.author: Old keeper — stone rubbing
notes.placement: Rubbing against the north wall in a central room; a faint static carved-foot motif, not a light effect.
notes.body: Ink can tell you where a path was. Feet can tell you where it is. Set the drawing beside the mark and listen with your toes. If nothing answers, leave the sheet for someone else. Copying it was still worth doing.

notes.author: Glimmer — keeper scrap
notes.placement: Keeper scrap on the north side of the western room; different ink from the Waystone rubbing.
notes.body: A glow mushroom can help you see the ground. It may also help something else see you. I used to hold one directly over my head. I have since developed a more considerate relationship with the dark.

notes.body: Three little ones. Three appetites. One path to the feeding beds. I drew the path very carefully, then used the margin to count their meals. The margin is full now. I should have drawn a smaller path.

notes.placement: Corrected field copy at the southeast edge of the upper eastern room; paper follows the wall, not a moving obstacle.
notes.body: Old Moss says I draw the hedges too straight. The hedges agree with him. I have stopped giving them corners and started marking the gaps between their roots. Those are what a traveller needs, after all.

notes.body: Six oilcloths, twelve lengths of cord, two spare lantern panes. Leave one bundle at every beach shelter. The crabs are carrying it above the tide. Do not offer them coins. They have asked for a dry place to sleep.

notes.body: I kept a copy of their stores list. Enough for the crossing, the inspection and the return. They expected to come back. I put the list on the high shelf because expecting a thing does not keep the tide out.

notes.body: Tail lost. Pride injured. Rest of lizard present and hungry. Have decided to call this a successful escape. Whoever finds this shelter next: the stone near the entrance keeps its warmth after sunset.

notes.body: Please leave the warm stones clear. Someone coming through may be colder than you are. If you have been lying on the best one all morning, there is probably enough warmth left for somebody else. I write this chiefly to remind myself.

notes.body: If the lantern goes dark, check for living glow bugs before you throw it away. A sheltered colony can wait a long time. I check this one every morning. It makes a small light when the lid is lifted.

notes.body: I tried to tell a sentinel that we might be late. It pointed to the warm stone beside its post. There is patience, and then there is whatever they have. I checked the stone before leaving. Still warm.

notes.body: The hiss tells you a jet is coming. Watch one full burst before choosing the crossing. Count the quiet as well as the noise. It is the quiet you will be walking through. These pipes have never been impressed by hurry.

notes.body: The smallest cap grew by the pool. I nearly brushed it away. Its children light the shelf now. At the Fairy Ring, three caps answer one another. Watch their order, then touch them with your tongue in the same order. They prefer a polite introduction.

notes.author: Gale — folded shelter slip
notes.placement: Shelter slip near the northeast room corner, outside any authored hazard cell; lightning still needs live testing.
notes.body: Sit beneath the ledge until you can feel your feet. Then choose the next ledge. Near the heights stands the struck oak. Its hollow shows a glint only when lightning comes. Look from shelter; nothing in a tree is worth forgetting where you are standing.

notes.body: Two lizards fit here if one stops complaining. Three fit if everyone leaves their packs outside. The roof holds through a hard storm. I have marked it for whoever comes after us. Bring the packs back in before leaving.

notes.body: The shallow route is not always a walking route. Wait and watch what the water uncovers. I once drew a perfectly good path while the tide was out, then forgot to mention the tide. This note is the correction.

notes.body: A mast shows through the reeds off Sun and Sea. The way to it waits for every star in the Tide Pools. I have kept the loose planks on shore. They tell us a boat broke. They do not tell us what happened to its travellers.
